concept.concept_description: Formalize one self-contained finite undirected multigraph development in Lean 4, with no entropy/compression material. Represent a multigraph by a finite edge type `E`, a finite vertex type `V`, and an endpoint map `ends : E → Sym2 V` (or an equivalent explicit unordered-pair encoding already convenient in Mathlib). Define a finite trail as a nonempty finite sequence of vertices together with a same-length-minus-one sequence of edges witnessing adjacency step-by-step, and require the edge sequence to be `Nodup`. Define, for a trail `T`, the incidence count at a vertex `v` to be the number of trail edges whose chosen step is incident to `v`. Prove the exact counting identity `∑ v, incidences(T,v) = 2 * T.edges.length`. Then define the endpoint imbalance `oddContribution(T,v)` as 1 if `v` is exactly one endpoint of the open trail and 0 otherwise, and prove the sharpened formula `incidences(T,v) = 2 * internalVisits(T,v) + oddContribution(T,v)`, where `internalVisits` counts interior occurrences of `v` in the vertex sequence. Derive the standard corollaries: every non-endpoint of a trail has even trail-incidence count, and the only possible odd trail-incidence vertices are the two endpoints; in particular, a closed trail has even trail-incidence count at every vertex. If time permits, package an Eulerian trail as a trail whose edge set is all edges of the graph exactly once, and deduce the usual necessary condition that a graph with an Eulerian trail has at most two vertices of odd degree, with zero odd-degree vertices in the closed case. The emphasis is on complete, typechecked proofs for this single pipeline.
concept.mathematical_framing: Every mathematical structure is a category, and every theorem is a natural transformation. Define the 'genome' of a mathematical theory as its category of models. Prove: two theories are Morita-equivalent iff their model categories are equivalent. Show: the 'mutation' of a theory (changing one axiom) corresponds to an adjunction between model categories. Conjecture: every 'evolutionary path' between theories can be decomposed into a sequence of adjunctions and quotients.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Entropy-Complexity Bridge: From Compression to Information Bounds

This file establishes formal bridges between algorithmic compression/complexity
and entropy-like information bounds on finite types. The central theme is:

> **Compression controls entropy-like support complexity.**
> If a finite family of objects can be injectively encoded into a bounded
> code space, then the family's cardinality (and hence its log-cardinality,
> a uniform entropy surrogate) is bounded by the code space size.

## Main Results

### Finite cardinality bounds from injective encodings
- `card_le_of_injective_to_fin`: Injective map to `Fin N` bounds cardinality by `N`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code`: Injective map to `Fin (2^k)` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode`: Injective map to `Fin k → Bool` bounds cardinality by `2^k`.
- `card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound`: Range of a map to `Fin (2^k)` has size ≤ `2^k`.

### Entropy bounds
- `EntropyBound`: Predicate `Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k`, the finite uniform entropy inequality.
- `entropyBound_of_injective_code`: Injective code implies entropy bound.
- `uniform_entropy_le_code_length`: Log-cardinality bounded by code length.

### Support monotonicity (data processing)
- `support_entropy_monotone_under_map`: `|range f| ≤ |α|`.
- `card_range_le_card_codomain`: `|range f| ≤ |β|`.
- `support_entropy_comp_monotone`: `|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|` — deterministic data processing.

### Cross-domain bridge
- `complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound`: Connects compressor bounds
  to finite cardinality control.

## Mathematical Significance

These theorems form the combinatorial skeleton of the source coding principle
and create a formal route from Kolmogorov-style complexity bounds to
entropy/information inequalities. The composition monotonicity theorem
`support_entropy_comp_monotone` is a combinatorial shadow of the
**data processing inequality**: deterministic post-processing cannot
increase the number of distinguishable outputs.
-/

open Set Function Finset Fintype

/-! ## Section 1: Core Finite Cardinality Bounds -/

/-- An injective map from a finite type to `Fin N` implies the source has
at most `N` elements. This is the fundamental counting principle underlying
all compression-to-entropy arguments. -/
theorem card_le_of_injective_to_fin
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {N : ℕ}
    (f : α → Fin N) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ N := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin N) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = N := Fintype.card_fin N

/-- An injective encoding into `Fin (2^k)` bounds source cardinality by `2^k`.
This is the exponential form of the entropy bound: if objects can be
described by `k`-bit codes, there are at most `2^k` of them. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k :=
  card_le_of_injective_to_fin enc henc

/-- The cardinality of the function space `Fin k → Bool` is exactly `2^k`.
This witnesses bitstrings of length `k` as a code space of size `2^k`. -/
theorem fintype_card_fun_bool (k : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) = 2^k := by
  simp [Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_bool]

/-- An injective encoding into explicit bitstrings `Fin k → Bool` bounds
cardinality by `2^k`. This is the most concrete form: each element gets
a unique `k`-bit string, so there can be at most `2^k` elements. -/
theorem card_le_two_pow_of_injective_bitcode
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (f : α → (Fin k → Bool)) (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card α ≤ Fintype.card (Fin k → Bool) := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hf
    _ = 2^k := fintype_card_fun_bool k

/-- The range of any map into `Fin (2^k)` has at most `2^k` elements.
This does not require injectivity — it bounds the number of distinguishable
outputs of any encoding scheme. -/
theorem card_range_le_two_pow_of_bitlength_bound
    {n k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin (2^k)) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ 2^k := by
  calc Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card (Fin (2^k)) := Fintype.card_subtype_le _
    _ = 2^k := Fintype.card_fin _

/-! ## Section 2: Entropy Bound Predicate and Logarithmic Form -/

/-- `EntropyBound α k` asserts that the uniform entropy of the finite type `α`
is at most `k` bits: equivalently, `|α| ≤ 2^k`. This is the finite
combinatorial skeleton of the source coding bound `H(X) ≤ k` for a
uniform source over `α` encoded with `k`-bit codewords. -/
def EntropyBound (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k

/-- An injective encoding into `k`-bit codes implies the entropy bound.
This is the formal finite-uniform entropy inequality: if every element
of `α` receives a unique `k`-bit code, then `H(α) ≤ k`. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_injective_code
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    EntropyBound α k :=
  card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc

/-
Logarithmic form of the entropy bound: if `α` injects into `Fin (2^k)`,
then `log₂ |α| ≤ k`. Uses `Nat.log` which is the floor of the logarithm.
-/
theorem uniform_entropy_le_code_length
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k := by
  -- We have card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code which gives Fintype.card α ≤ 2^k.
  -- Taking the base-2 logarithm is monotonic, so log₂ |α| ≤ log₂ 2^k = k.
  have hcard : Fintype.card α ≤ 2 ^ k := by
    apply card_le_two_pow_of_injective_code enc henc
  exact (Nat.log_mono_right hcard).trans (Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k).le

/-- For any injective encoding `α → Fin (2^k)`, the
log-cardinality of `α` is bounded by `k`. -/
theorem log_card_range_le_of_embedding_into_bitstrings
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (enc : α → Fin (2^k)) (henc : Function.Injective enc) :
    Nat.log 2 (Fintype.card α) ≤ k :=
  uniform_entropy_le_code_length enc henc

/-! ## Section 3: Support Monotonicity — Data Processing -/

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as its domain.
This is a combinatorial form of the principle that deterministic
processing cannot create new distinguishable outputs. -/
theorem support_entropy_monotone_under_map
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card α :=
  Fintype.card_range_le f

/-- The range of a map has at most as many elements as the codomain.
This is the trivial but useful fact that range ⊆ codomain implies
the cardinality inequality. -/
theorem card_range_le_card_codomain
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    (f : α → β) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range f) ≤ Fintype.card β :=
  Fintype.card_subtype_le _

/-
**Combinatorial Data Processing Inequality.**
Composition cannot increase the number of distinguishable outputs:
`|range (g ∘ f)| ≤ |range f|`. This is the finite combinatorial
shadow of the data processing inequality `H(g(X)) ≤ H(X)` for
deterministic channels.
-/
theorem support_entropy_comp_monotone
    {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    Fintype.card (Set.range (g ∘ f)) ≤ Fintype.card (Set.range f) := by
  -- By definition of range, we know that every element in the range of `g ∘ f` is of the form `g (f a)` for some `a ∈ α`.
  have h_range : Set.range (g ∘ f) = g '' Set.range f := by
    grind +splitIndPred;
  simp +decide only [h_range, card_ofFinset];
  refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_image_le ) _;
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun x hx => by aesop;

/-! ## Section 4: Compression Lower Bounds -/

/-
If a type has more than `2^k` elements, no injective encoding into
`k`-bit codes exists. This is the compression impossibility theorem:
you cannot losslessly compress a family of size `> 2^k` into `k` bits.
-/
theorem no_injective_code_of_card_gt
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
    (hcard : 2^k < Fintype.card α) :
    ¬ ∃ f : α → Fin (2^k), Function.Injective f := by
  exact fun ⟨ f, hf ⟩ => not_le_of_gt hcard ( card_le_of_injective_to_fin f hf )

/-! ## Section 5: Subadditivity Under Products -/

/-
Product encoding: if `α` has at most `2^k` elements and `β` has at most
`2^ℓ` elements, then `α × β` has at most `2^(k + ℓ)` elements.
This is entropy subadditivity: `H(X, Y) ≤ H(X) + H(Y)`.
-/
theorem entropyBound_prod_of_entropyBound
    {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] {k ℓ : ℕ}
    (hα : EntropyBound α k) (hβ : EntropyBound β ℓ) :
    EntropyBound (α × β) (k + ℓ) := by
  unfold EntropyBound at *;
  simpa only [ pow_add, Fintype.card_prod ] using Nat.mul_le_mul hα hβ

/-! ## Section 6: Cross-Domain Bridge to Compression-Complexity -/

namespace EntropyComplexityBridge

/-- An invertible compressor with idempotence, length-bounding, and inverse. -/
structure InvertibleCompressor where
  compress : List Bool → List Bool
  decompress : List Bool → List Bool
  hidem : ∀ s, compress (compress s) = compress s
  hlen : ∀ s, (compress s).length ≤ s.length
  hstrict : ∀ s, compress s ≠ s → (compress s).length < s.length
  hinv : ∀ s, decompress (compress s) = s

/-
**Complexity bound implies finite entropy bound (bridge theorem).**

Given an invertible compressor `C` and a finite family of binary strings,
if every element has compressed length ≤ `k`, then the family has at most
`2^(k+1)` elements (since there are `2^(k+1) - 1` binary strings of
length ≤ `k`).

This is the key bridge: algorithmic complexity upper bounds (via compressors)
imply entropy upper bounds (via cardinality control).
-/
theorem complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    Fintype.card α ≤ 2^(k+1) := by
  -- We know that `compress` is injective and its image is contained in the set of lists of length ≤ k.
  have h_image : Finset.card (Finset.image (fun a => C.compress (embed a)) Finset.univ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
    -- The set of lists of length ≤ k is finite and has cardinality 2^(k+1) - 1.
    have h_card : Finset.card (Finset.filter (fun l => l.length ≤ k) (Finset.biUnion (Finset.range (k + 1)) (fun i => Finset.image (fun l : Fin i → Bool => List.ofFn l) (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin i → Bool)))) ) ≤ 2^(k+1) - 1 := by
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_filter_le _ _ ) _;
      refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _;
      rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun x y hxy => by simpa [ funext_iff ] using hxy ] ; simp +decide [ Nat.geomSum_eq ];
    refine' le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card _ ) h_card;
    simp +decide [ Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact fun a => ⟨ ⟨ _, hbound a, fun i => ( C.compress ( embed a ) |> List.get <| ⟨ i, by linarith [ hbound a, i.2 ] ⟩ ), by simp +decide ⟩, hbound a ⟩;
  rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injective _ fun a b hab => hembed <| by have := C.hinv ( embed a ) ; have := C.hinv ( embed b ) ; aesop ] at h_image ; exact le_trans h_image ( Nat.sub_le _ _ )

/-- **Finite family complexity certificate.**
If a compressor certifies that every element of a finite type has
compressed representation of length ≤ `k`, this yields an entropy
bound on the type. -/
theorem entropyBound_of_compressor
    (C : InvertibleCompressor)
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (embed : α → List Bool)
    (hembed : Function.Injective embed)
    {k : ℕ}
    (hbound : ∀ a : α, (C.compress (embed a)).length ≤ k) :
    EntropyBound α (k + 1) :=
  complexity_bound_implies_finite_entropy_bound C embed hembed hbound

end EntropyComplexityBridge

/-
  # Eulerian Trails in Finite Undirected Multigraphs

  A self-contained development of Eulerian trails in finite undirected
  multigraphs, with no category-theoretic content.

  ## Representation

  A multigraph is given by a vertex type `V`, an edge type `E`, and two
  endpoint maps `fst, snd : E → V`.  The graph is *undirected*: the orientation
  of an edge is irrelevant and is only used to talk about traversals.  Loops
  (edges with `fst e = snd e`) are allowed and contribute `2` to a vertex
  degree, and parallel edges are allowed since `E` is an arbitrary type.

  A *walk* is a starting vertex together with a list of steps `(e, v)`, each
  meaning "traverse edge `e`, arriving at `v`".  A walk is *valid* if every
  edge actually connects its two consecutive vertices (in either orientation).
  A *trail* additionally uses no edge twice, and an *Eulerian trail* uses every
  edge exactly once.

  ## Main results

  * `Multigraph.incidence_count_identity` — the core incidence identity:
    for any valid walk, the total endpoint-incidence at a vertex `w` plus the
    start/end correction terms equals twice the number of times `w` is visited.
  * `Multigraph.degree_add_endpoints` — the specialization to Eulerian trails:
    `degree w + [s = w] + [t = w] = 2 * (visits of w)`.
  * `Multigraph.even_degree_of_ne_endpoints` — every non-endpoint vertex has
    even degree.
  * `Multigraph.odd_degree_card_le_two` — a multigraph with an Eulerian trail
    has at most two odd-degree vertices.
  * `Multigraph.all_even_of_closed` — for a closed Eulerian trail (`s = t`),
    every vertex has even degree.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace EulerianMultigraph

open Finset

/-- A finite undirected multigraph: a vertex type, an edge type, and two
endpoint maps.  Orientation is irrelevant for the undirected structure; it is
only used to describe traversals. -/
structure Multigraph (V : Type*) (E : Type*) where
  /-- One endpoint of each edge. -/
  fst : E → V
  /-- The other endpoint of each edge. -/
  snd : E → V

variable {V : Type*} {E : Type*}

/-- The list of edges used by a sequence of steps. -/
def usedEdges (steps : List (E × V)) : List E := steps.map Prod.fst

namespace Multigraph

/-- Edge `e` connects vertices `a` and `b` (in either orientation). -/
def Connects (G : Multigraph V E) (e : E) (a b : V) : Prop :=
  (G.fst e = a ∧ G.snd e = b) ∨ (G.fst e = b ∧ G.snd e = a)

/-- A walk starting at `a` and following the given steps is *valid* if every
edge connects its two consecutive vertices. -/
def IsValidWalk (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | a, (e, b) :: rest => G.Connects e a b ∧ G.IsValidWalk b rest

/-- The list of vertices visited by a walk starting at `a`. -/
def visited (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → List V
  | a, [] => [a]
  | a, (_, b) :: rest => a :: G.visited b rest

/-- The final vertex of a walk starting at `a`. -/
def endVertex (G : Multigraph V E) : V → List (E × V) → V
  | a, [] => a
  | _, (_, b) :: rest => G.endVertex b rest

variable (G : Multigraph V E)

/-- The total endpoint-incidence of the edges used by a walk at the vertex `w`:
each used edge contributes `1` for each of its endpoints equal to `w` (so a loop
at `w` contributes `2`). -/
def edgeIncidenceSum [DecidableEq V] (w : V) (steps : List (E × V)) : ℕ :=
  ((usedEdges steps).map
    (fun e => (if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0) + (if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0))).sum

/-- The degree of a vertex `w`: the number of edge-endpoints equal to `w`,
counting loops twice. -/
def degree [DecidableEq V] [Fintype E] (w : V) : ℕ :=
  ∑ e : E, ((if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0) + (if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0))

/-- An Eulerian trail from `s` to `t`: a valid walk ending at `t` that uses
every edge exactly once. -/
def IsEulerianTrail [DecidableEq E] (s t : V) (steps : List (E × V)) : Prop :=
  G.IsValidWalk s steps ∧ G.endVertex s steps = t ∧
    ∀ e : E, (usedEdges steps).count e = 1

/-- A multigraph *has* an Eulerian trail from `s` to `t`. -/
def HasEulerianTrail [DecidableEq E] (s t : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ steps, G.IsEulerianTrail s t steps

/-! ### The core incidence identity -/

/-- **Core incidence identity.**  For any valid walk starting at `a`, the total
endpoint-incidence at a vertex `w` over the used edges, plus a `1` for each of
the start vertex `a` and the end vertex equal to `w`, equals twice the number of
times `w` is visited.  Intuitively, each visit to `w` consumes two incidences
(one to enter, one to leave) except that the start and end vertices have one
unmatched incidence each. -/
theorem incidence_count_identity [DecidableEq V] (w : V) :
    ∀ (a : V) (steps : List (E × V)), G.IsValidWalk a steps →
      G.edgeIncidenceSum w steps + (if a = w then 1 else 0)
          + (if G.endVertex a steps = w then 1 else 0)
        = 2 * (G.visited a steps).count w := by
  intro a steps h;
  induction' steps with e steps ih generalizing a; all_goals grind +locals

/-! ### From the incidence identity to degrees -/

/-- For a walk that uses every edge exactly once, the endpoint-incidence sum at
`w` equals the degree of `w`. -/
theorem edgeIncidenceSum_eq_degree [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] (w : V)
    (steps : List (E × V)) (h : ∀ e : E, (usedEdges steps).count e = 1) :
    G.edgeIncidenceSum w steps = G.degree w := by
  have h_finset : (usedEdges steps).toFinset = Finset.univ := by
    exact Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun e => List.mem_toFinset.mpr ( List.count_pos_iff.mp ( by linarith [ h e ] ) );
  convert Finset.sum_list_map_count ( usedEdges steps ) ( fun e => ( if G.fst e = w then 1 else 0 ) + ( if G.snd e = w then 1 else 0 ) ) using 1;
  aesop

/-- **Degree identity for Eulerian trails.**  If `steps` is an Eulerian trail
from `s` to `t`, then for every vertex `w`,
`degree w + [s = w] + [t = w] = 2 * (number of visits of w)`. -/
theorem degree_add_endpoints [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t w : V}
    {steps : List (E × V)} (h : G.IsEulerianTrail s t steps) :
    G.degree w + (if s = w then 1 else 0) + (if t = w then 1 else 0)
      = 2 * (G.visited s steps).count w := by
  convert incidence_count_identity G w s steps h.1 using 1;
  rw [ edgeIncidenceSum_eq_degree G w steps h.2.2, h.2.1 ]

/-! ### Parity consequences -/

/-- Every vertex other than the two endpoints of an Eulerian trail has even
degree. -/
theorem even_degree_of_ne_endpoints [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq E] [Fintype E] {s t w : V}

import Mathlib

/-!
# A Finite Ecosystem-Equilibrium Model of Theories

This file develops a small, completely finite, combinatorial optimization model of an
*ecosystem of theories*.  The picture is the following.

* A finite type `T` enumerates a collection of *theories* (or theory-states).
* Each theory carries three natural-number invariants:
  `connections t` (how many other theories it links to), `proofDensity t`
  (a coarse measure of how much is proved per unit of structure), and
  `axiomCount t` (the size of its axiomatic base, always positive).
* The *fitness* of a theory is the rational number
  `fitness t = (connections t * proofDensity t) / axiomCount t`:
  a theory is fitter when it is well connected and proof-dense relative to the
  number of assumptions it must postulate.
* A finite type `N` enumerates *ecological niches*.  A map `niche : T → N` assigns
  each theory to a niche.
* A finite set of theories `E` is *at equilibrium* (`AtEquilibrium E niche`) when
  distinct surviving theories occupy distinct niches, i.e. `niche` is injective on
  `E`.  This is the competitive-exclusion principle: two theories cannot stably
  coexist in the same niche.

The mathematical content is a clean finite optimization theory:

* **Well-definedness / positivity.**  The denominator `axiomCount t` is nonzero and
  `fitness` is always nonnegative.
* **Carrying capacity.**  An equilibrium set has at most `Fintype.card N` members
  (`card_le_card_niche`), and conversely any set larger than the number of niches
  cannot be at equilibrium (`not_atEquilibrium_of_card_lt`).
* **Aggregate fitness bounds.**  If every member of `E` clears a fitness threshold
  `q`, then the total fitness is at least `E.card • q`, and the *average* fitness is
  at least `q`.
* **Constructive niche selection.**  Given a candidate pool `C`, `selectByNiche`
  picks, in each occupied niche, the theory of maximal fitness.  The selected set is
  contained in `C`, is at equilibrium, has at most `Fintype.card N` members, and the
  chosen representative of a niche fitness-dominates every candidate in that niche.
* **Uniqueness under strict dominance.**  If each occupied niche has a *unique*
  fitness-maximizer, then `selectByNiche C niche` is the *only* equilibrium subset of
  `C` that occupies every occupied niche by a nichewise maximizer.

Everything is finite and is proved from standard `Finset`/`Fintype` cardinality
infrastructure.  No logarithms, entropy, or compression machinery is involved.
-/

namespace EcosystemEquilibrium

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

variable {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
variable {N : Type*} [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N]

/-! ## Fitness -/

/-- The fitness of a theory: connectivity times proof-density per axiom. -/
def fitness (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ) (t : T) : ℚ :=
  ((connections t : ℚ) * (proofDensity t : ℚ)) / (axiomCount t : ℚ)

variable {connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ}

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- The denominator of `fitness` is nonzero, given a positive axiom count. -/
lemma axiomCount_cast_ne_zero (hax : ∀ t, 0 < axiomCount t) (t : T) :
    (axiomCount t : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr ( ne_of_gt ( hax t ) )

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Fitness is always nonnegative. -/
lemma fitness_nonneg (t : T) : 0 ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t := by
  exact div_nonneg ( mul_nonneg ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ ) ) ( Nat.cast_nonneg _ )

/-! ## Equilibrium and carrying capacity -/

/-- A finite set of theories is *at equilibrium* when distinct surviving theories
occupy distinct niches: `niche` is injective on `E`. -/
def AtEquilibrium (E : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Prop :=
  Set.InjOn niche (↑E : Set T)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Carrying capacity: an equilibrium set has at most as many members as there are
niches. -/
theorem card_le_card_niche {E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (h : AtEquilibrium E niche) : E.card ≤ Fintype.card N := by
      exact Finset.card_le_card ( show E.image niche ⊆ Finset.univ from Finset.subset_univ _ ) |> le_trans ( by rw [ Finset.card_image_of_injOn h ] )

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- Pigeonhole converse: a set larger than the number of niches cannot be at
equilibrium. -/
theorem not_atEquilibrium_of_card_lt {E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (h : Fintype.card N < E.card) : ¬ AtEquilibrium E niche :=
  fun he => absurd (card_le_card_niche he) (not_le.mpr h)

/-! ## Aggregate fitness bounds -/

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- If every member of `E` has fitness at least `q`, the total fitness is at least
`E.card • q`. -/
theorem card_nsmul_le_sum_fitness {E : Finset T} {q : ℚ}
    (h : ∀ t ∈ E, q ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) :
    E.card • q ≤ ∑ t ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t :=
  Finset.card_nsmul_le_sum E _ q h

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] in
/-- If every member of a nonempty `E` has fitness at least `q`, the *average*
fitness is at least `q`. -/
theorem le_avg_fitness {E : Finset T} {q : ℚ} (hE : E.Nonempty)
    (h : ∀ t ∈ E, q ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) :
    q ≤ (∑ t ∈ E, fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount t) / (E.card : ℚ) := by
  rw [ le_div_iff₀ ( Nat.cast_pos.mpr hE.card_pos ) ];
  simpa [ mul_comm ] using card_nsmul_le_sum_fitness h

/-! ## Constructive niche selection -/

/-- Candidates in pool `C` that live in niche `n`. -/
def nicheCandidates (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) (n : N) : Finset T :=
  C.filter (fun t => niche t = n)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
@[simp] lemma mem_nicheCandidates {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N} {t : T} :
    t ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n ↔ t ∈ C ∧ niche t = n := by
  exact Finset.mem_filter

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The niche of any candidate `t ∈ C` is occupied: its own niche-candidate set is
nonempty. -/
lemma nicheCandidates_nonempty_self {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {t : T}
    (ht : t ∈ C) : (nicheCandidates C niche (niche t)).Nonempty :=
  ⟨t, mem_nicheCandidates.mpr ⟨ht, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The maximal-fitness representative of an occupied niche `n` in pool `C`. -/
noncomputable def nicheRepresentative (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) (n : N)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) : T :=
  Classical.choose (Finset.exists_max_image (nicheCandidates C niche n)
    (fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount) h)

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
lemma nicheRepresentative_mem {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈
      nicheCandidates C niche n := by
  exact Classical.choose_spec ( Finset.exists_max_image _ _ h ) |>.1

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
lemma nicheRepresentative_max {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    ∀ x ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount x ≤
        fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount
          (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) := by
  exact Classical.choose_spec ( Finset.exists_max_image _ _ h ) |>.2

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The representative of niche `n` indeed lies in `n`. -/
lemma nicheRepresentative_niche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    niche (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) = n :=
  (mem_nicheCandidates.mp (nicheRepresentative_mem h)).2

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The representative of niche `n` lies in the pool `C`. -/
lemma nicheRepresentative_mem_pool {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈ C :=
  (mem_nicheCandidates.mp (nicheRepresentative_mem h)).1

/-- The selected ecosystem: one maximal-fitness representative per occupied niche. -/
noncomputable def selectByNiche (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Finset T :=
  C.attach.image (fun p =>
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche p.1)
      (nicheCandidates_nonempty_self p.2))

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Every selected theory lies in the candidate pool. -/
theorem selectByNiche_subset {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche ⊆ C := by
  intro y hy; rw [selectByNiche, Finset.mem_image] at hy; obtain ⟨p, _, rfl⟩ := hy; exact nicheRepresentative_mem_pool _;

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- If `y` is selected, then it is the canonical representative of its own niche
(for any nonemptiness witness). -/
lemma selectByNiche_eq_rep {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {y : T}
    (hy : y ∈ selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche (niche y)).Nonempty) :
    y = nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche y) h := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : C, nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche (niche p.1) (nicheCandidates_nonempty_self p.2) = y := by
    unfold selectByNiche at hy; aesop;
  grind +suggestions

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The niche of a selected theory is occupied in `C`. -/
lemma selectByNiche_niche_mem_image {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {y : T}
    (hy : y ∈ selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche) :
    niche y ∈ C.image niche := by
  convert Finset.mem_image_of_mem niche ( selectByNiche_subset hy ) using 1

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Selected theories occupy distinct niches: the selection is at equilibrium. -/
theorem atEquilibrium_selectByNiche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    AtEquilibrium (selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche) niche := by
  intro a ha b hb hab;
  grind +locals

omit [Fintype T] in
/-- The selected ecosystem respects the carrying capacity. -/
theorem card_selectByNiche_le {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} :
    (selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche).card ≤ Fintype.card N :=
  card_le_card_niche atEquilibrium_selectByNiche

omit [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Optimality of the selection: in each occupied niche the chosen representative
fitness-dominates every candidate of that niche. -/
theorem fitness_le_representative {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {x : T} {n : N}
    (hx : x ∈ C) (hxn : niche x = n)
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount x ≤
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount
        (nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h) :=
  nicheRepresentative_max h x (mem_nicheCandidates.mpr ⟨hx, hxn⟩)

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- The chosen representative is itself selected. -/
theorem nicheRepresentative_mem_selectByNiche {C : Finset T} {niche : T → N} {n : N}
    (h : (nicheCandidates C niche n).Nonempty) :
    nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche n h ∈
      selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : ∃ t, t ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n := by
    exact h;
  refine' Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨ ⟨ t, Finset.mem_filter.mp ht |>.1 ⟩, _, _ ⟩ <;> simp_all +decide [ nicheCandidates ];
  congr! 1;
  exact Finset.mem_filter.mp ht |>.2

/-! ## Uniqueness under strict dominance -/

/-- The hypothesis that within each niche of the pool `C` the fitness-maximizer is
unique: any two maximizers of the same niche coincide. -/
def UniqueNicheMaximizer (connections proofDensity axiomCount : T → ℕ)
    (C : Finset T) (niche : T → N) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : N) (a b : T), a ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n → b ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n →
    (∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount a) →
    (∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche n,
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤ fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount b) →
    a = b

omit [Fintype T] [Fintype N] in
/-- Uniqueness: under unique niche-maximizers, `selectByNiche C niche` is the only
equilibrium subset of `C` that covers every occupied niche with a nichewise
fitness-maximizer.

* `hsub : E ⊆ C` — survivors are drawn from the pool;
* `_heq : AtEquilibrium E niche` — the survivors form an equilibrium (this was part
  of the requested hypotheses; it is in fact logically redundant here, since the
  conclusion `E = selectByNiche ...` already forces equilibrium, so the proof does
  not use it);
* `hcover : E.image niche = C.image niche` — exactly the occupied niches are
  represented (one each, by the equilibrium condition);
* `hmax` — every survivor is a fitness-maximizer of its niche. -/
theorem eq_selectByNiche_of_unique {C E : Finset T} {niche : T → N}
    (huniq : UniqueNicheMaximizer connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche)
    (hsub : E ⊆ C)
    (_heq : AtEquilibrium E niche)
    (hcover : E.image niche = C.image niche)
    (hmax : ∀ e ∈ E, ∀ s ∈ nicheCandidates C niche (niche e),
      fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount s ≤
        fitness connections proofDensity axiomCount e) :
    E = selectByNiche connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche := by
  ext; simp [selectByNiche];
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · use ‹_›;
    exact ⟨ hsub h, huniq _ _ _ ( nicheRepresentative_mem _ ) ( by aesop ) ( nicheRepresentative_max _ ) ( hmax _ h ) ⟩;
  · obtain ⟨ a, ha, rfl ⟩ := h;
    obtain ⟨ e, he, he' ⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp ( hcover.symm ▸ Finset.mem_image_of_mem niche ha );
    have := huniq ( niche a ) e ( nicheRepresentative connections proofDensity axiomCount C niche ( niche a ) ( nicheCandidates_nonempty_self ha ) ) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> simp_all +decide [ nicheCandidates ];
    · exact hsub he;
    · exact ⟨ nicheRepresentative_mem_pool _, nicheRepresentative_niche _ ⟩;
    · grind +suggestions

end EcosystemEquilibrium

falsifiable conjecture about the fitness model
`f(T) = connections(T) · proofDensity(T) / axiomCount(T)`.

---

## 1. Selection pressure toward *primitive* (irreducible) theories

**Conjecture.** Under any fitness-improving evolution, the long-run population is
dominated by theories that are not Rankin–Selberg-type products of smaller
theories; composite theories are an evolutionary dead end.

The key insight is that `selberg_product_fitness_subadditive` shows the conductor
(axiomatic cost) *multiplies* under composition while the degree (connection
count) only *adds*, so `f(S₁ × S₂) ≤ f(S₁) + f(S₂)` with strict loss whenever both
factors are non-trivial — composition can never create fitness, only dilute it.

Why now? We already have the Selberg census `product` operation formalized and the
subadditivity inequality proved, so the next step (defining a primitivity
predicate and proving products are strictly sub-apex) is directly within reach
rather than speculative.

---

**Conjecture.** For any finite niche space `N`, every ecosystem at equilibrium has

realizing exactly `card N` distinct foundational theories.

section of the niche map, turning the inequality into an exact carrying-capacity

`c·d·axioms(T) > connections(T)·proofDensity(T)·(axioms(T)+a)` — there is a sharp
threshold separating "fertile" axioms (large cardinals) from "sterile" ones.

open Computability

namespace AutomaticSequences

variable {α σ β : Type*}

/-- The **output DFA** for a target value `z`: same transitions as `M`, but the
accepting states are exactly those whose output label is `z`.  Its language is the
set of words mapped to `z`. -/
def outputValueDFA (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β) : DFA α σ :=
  { M with accept := {q | out q = z} }

@[simp] theorem mem_outputValueDFA_accepts (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β)
    (w : List α) :
    w ∈ (outputValueDFA M out z).accepts ↔ out (M.eval w) = z := by
  rw [DFA.mem_accepts]; rfl

theorem outputValueDFA_accepts_eq (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β) :
    (outputValueDFA M out z).accepts = {w | out (M.eval w) = z} := by
  rfl

/-- **Automatic sequences are finite-valued.**  Whatever the digit-representation
function `repr`, the sequence `n ↦ out (M.eval (repr n))` has finite range,
because the output map factors through the finite state set. -/
theorem autoSeq_range_finite [Finite σ] (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β)
    (repr : ℕ → List α) :
    (Set.range (fun n => out (M.eval (repr n)))).Finite := by
  apply Set.Finite.subset (Set.finite_range out)
  rintro y ⟨n, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨_, rfl⟩

/-- **The identity sequence is not automatic.**  No finite-state DFAO over any
representation can output `a_n = n` for all `n`: any candidate disagrees at some
index.  This refutes the conjecture "integer polynomial-recurrence ⟹ automatic":
`a_n = n` obeys `a_{n+1} = a_n + 1` yet is unbounded. -/
theorem id_not_automatic {σ : Type*} [Finite σ] (M : DFA ℕ σ) (out : σ → ℕ)
    (repr : ℕ → List ℕ) :
    ∃ n, out (M.eval (repr n)) ≠ n := by
  by_contra h
  push_neg at h
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (fun n => out (M.eval (repr n))) := fun y => ⟨y, h y⟩
  have hfin : (Set.range (fun n => out (M.eval (repr n)))).Finite :=
    autoSeq_range_finite M out repr
  rw [hsurj.range_eq] at hfin
  exact Set.infinite_univ hfin

/-- **Decidability of the zero-in-sequence problem (finite-search reduction).**
A target value `z` occurs as some `out (M.eval w)` iff it occurs for a word of
length below the state count.  The infinite search becomes a finite one. -/
theorem zero_value_iff_short [Fintype σ] (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β) :
    (∃ w, out (M.eval w) = z) ↔
      (∃ w, out (M.eval w) = z ∧ w.length < Fintype.card σ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
    have hne : (outputValueDFA M out z).accepts.Nonempty :=
      ⟨w, by rw [mem_outputValueDFA_accepts]; exact hw⟩
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hlt⟩ := exists_short_of_accepts (outputValueDFA M out z) hne
    rw [mem_outputValueDFA_accepts] at hx
    exact ⟨x, hx, hlt⟩
  · rintro ⟨w, hw, -⟩; exact ⟨w, hw⟩

/-- **Zero infinitely often.**  If a value `z` is attained by a word at least as
long as the number of states, it is attained by infinitely many words. -/
theorem zero_value_infinite [Fintype σ] (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β)
    (h : ∃ w, out (M.eval w) = z ∧ Fintype.card σ ≤ w.length) :
    {w | out (M.eval w) = z}.Infinite := by
  obtain ⟨w, hw, hlen⟩ := h
  have hmem : w ∈ (outputValueDFA M out z).accepts := by
    rw [mem_outputValueDFA_accepts]; exact hw
  have := accepts_infinite_of_long (outputValueDFA M out z) hmem hlen
  rwa [outputValueDFA_accepts_eq] at this

/-- **Decidable instance** for the existence of a word with a given output value
(the zero-in-sequence problem), assuming a finite alphabet and decidable
equality. -/
instance decidableExistsOutputValue [Fintype σ] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [DecidableEq β] (M : DFA α σ) (out : σ → β) (z : β) :
    Decidable (∃ w, out (M.eval w) = z) := by
  haveI : DecidablePred (· ∈ (outputValueDFA M out z).accept) :=
    fun q => decidable_of_iff (out q = z) Iff.rfl
  refine decidable_of_iff (outputValueDFA M out z).accepts.Nonempty ?_
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨w, hw⟩; rw [mem_outputValueDFA_accepts] at hw; exact ⟨w, hw⟩

Restricting an automaton to a single repeated letter `a` makes the run iterate
the endofunction `s ↦ M.step s a`.  In the finite monoid `Function.End σ` this
iteration is eventually periodic — exactly the catalog result

theorem End_pow_apply (f : Function.End σ) (n : ℕ) (x : σ) :
    (f ^ n) x = f^[n] x := by
  induction n generalizing x with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [pow_succ, Function.iterate_succ]
    show (f ^ k) (f x) = f^[k] (f x)
    rw [ih]

theorem evalFrom_replicate (M : DFA α σ) (q : σ) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
    M.evalFrom q (List.replicate n a) = (fun s => M.step s a)^[n] q := by
  induction n generalizing q with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    show M.evalFrom (M.step q a) (List.replicate k a) = _
    rw [ih]

`f = (s ↦ M.step s a) : Function.End σ`, the sequence
`n ↦ out (M.eval (List.replicate n a))` is eventually periodic. -/
theorem unary_autoSeq_eventually_periodic [Finite σ] (M : DFA α σ) (a : α)
    (out : σ → β) :
    ∃ N T : ℕ, 0 < T ∧ ∀ n, N ≤ n →
      out (M.eval (List.replicate (n + T) a)) =
        out (M.eval (List.replicate n a)) := by
  haveI : Finite (Function.End σ) := inferInstanceAs (Finite (σ → σ))
  obtain ⟨N, T, hT, hper⟩ := pow_eventually_periodic
    (M := Function.End σ) (fun s => M.step s a)
  refine ⟨N, T, hT, fun n hn => ?_⟩
  have hpt := hper n hn
  have key : M.eval (List.replicate (n + T) a) = M.eval (List.replicate n a) := by
    show M.evalFrom M.start (List.replicate (n + T) a) =
      M.evalFrom M.start (List.replicate n a)
    rw [evalFrom_replicate, evalFrom_replicate, ← End_pow_apply, ← End_pow_apply, hpt]
  rw [key]

/-!
# The Zero-in-Sequence Problem for Automatic Sequences: DFA Emptiness Core

This file develops the decidability core underlying the *zero-in-sequence problem*
for `k`-automatic sequences.  An automatic sequence `(a_n)` is computed by a
deterministic finite automaton reading the base-`k` digits of `n`; the question
"does there exist `n` with `a_n = 0`?" reduces to *language emptiness* for a
derived DFA whose accepting states are exactly the output-zero states.

The mathematical heart of the matter is a pigeonhole/pumping argument:

* **Short witness** (`exists_short_of_accepts`): if a DFA with `s` states accepts
  *any* word, it accepts a word of length `< s`.  Hence the (a priori infinite)
  search for an accepted word reduces to a *finite* search — this is the
  decidability algorithm.

* **Infinitude** (`accepts_infinite_of_long`): if a DFA accepts a word of length
  `≥ s`, it accepts infinitely many words.  This is the precise sense in which
  "if the DFA accepts any long string, `a_n = 0` infinitely often".

* **Finite reduction / decidability** (`accepts_nonempty_iff_short`,
  `decidableAcceptsNonempty`): nonemptiness of the accepted language is
  equivalent to a bounded finite search, hence decidable.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--

## Hypothesis (Hypothesizer)
H1: For a DFA with `s` states, acceptance of *some* word forces acceptance of a
    *short* word (length `< s`).  [Decidability of emptiness.]
H2: Acceptance of a *long* word (length `≥ s`) forces acceptance of *infinitely*
    many words.  [The "zero infinitely often" phenomenon.]
H3 (surprising): the dividing line between "finite acceptance" and "infinite
    acceptance" is exactly the state count `s` — there is no intermediate regime.

## Experiment (Experimenter)
Formalized over Mathlib's `DFA`.  H1 proved by minimal-length descent powered by
`DFA.pumping_lemma` (pump *down*: drop the loop `b`).  H2 proved by pumping *up*:
the injection `i ↦ a ++ bⁱ ++ c` lands in the language with strictly increasing
lengths.  H3 packaged as the `Finite ↔ no long word` characterization.

## Analysis (Analyst)
All three survive.  The key structural fact is that `b ≠ []` in the pumping
decomposition: it makes the down-pump *strictly* shorten and the up-pump
*strictly* lengthen, which is what powers both directions.

## Critique (Critic)
Counterexample probe: could a DFA accept finitely many words yet some of length
`≥ s`?  No — `accepts_infinite_of_long` rules this out; the explicit injection is
the certificate.  Could the short-witness bound be off by one?  We use `< s`
(strict), matching that a word of length `≥ s` triggers pumping.  Edge case: the
empty language has no witnesses and `accepts_nonempty_iff_short` correctly reports
`False ↔ False`.

## Synthesis (PI)
`decidableAcceptsNonempty` turns the bounded search into an actual `Decidable`
instance, i.e. the zero-in-sequence problem is algorithmically decidable.

open Computability

namespace AutomaticSequences

variable {α : Type*} {σ : Type*} (M : DFA α σ) [Fintype σ]

/--
**Down-pump.** If a DFA accepts a word of length at least its state count,
it accepts a strictly shorter word.
-/
theorem exists_shorter_of_long {x : List α} (hx : x ∈ M.accepts)
    (hlen : Fintype.card σ ≤ x.length) :
    ∃ y ∈ M.accepts, y.length < x.length := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, hx_decomp, habc⟩ : ∃ a b c, x = a ++ b ++ c ∧ a.length + b.length ≤ Fintype.card σ ∧ b ≠ [] ∧ {a} * {b}∗ * {c} ≤ M.accepts := by
    convert M.pumping_lemma hx hlen using 1;
  refine' ⟨ a ++ c, _, _ ⟩;
  · have := habc.2.2;
    convert this _;
    simp +decide [ Language.mul_def ];
    exact ⟨ a, rfl, [ ], Language.nil_mem_kstar _, c, rfl, by simp +decide ⟩;
  · simp +arith +decide [ hx_decomp ];
    exact List.length_pos_iff.mpr habc.2.1

/--
**Short witness.** If a DFA accepts any word, it accepts one of length less
than the number of states.  This is the finite-search reduction that makes
language emptiness (hence the zero-in-sequence problem) decidable.
-/
theorem exists_short_of_accepts (h : M.accepts.Nonempty) :
    ∃ x ∈ M.accepts, x.length < Fintype.card σ := by
  -- By induction on the length of the words in the accepted set, we can show that there exists a word of length at most (Fintype.card σ) - 1 in the accepted set.
  have h_ind : ∀ x ∈ M.accepts, ∃ y ∈ M.accepts, y.length < Fintype.card σ := by
    intro x hx
    induction' n : x.length using Nat.strong_induction_on with n ih generalizing x;
    by_cases hlen : Fintype.card σ ≤ x.length;
    · obtain ⟨ y, hy, hy' ⟩ := exists_shorter_of_long M hx hlen;
      exact ih _ ( by linarith ) _ hy rfl;
    · exact ⟨ x, hx, lt_of_not_ge hlen ⟩;
  exact h_ind _ h.choose_spec

/-- **Decidability reduction.** Nonemptiness of the accepted language is
equivalent to a bounded, finite search. -/
theorem accepts_nonempty_iff_short :
    M.accepts.Nonempty ↔ ∃ x ∈ M.accepts, x.length < Fintype.card σ := by
  constructor
  · exact exists_short_of_accepts M
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, -⟩; exact ⟨x, hx⟩

/--
**Up-pump / infinitude.** If a DFA accepts a word at least as long as its
state count, it accepts infinitely many words.  This is the formal version of
"if the automaton accepts a long string, then `a_n = 0` for infinitely many
`n`".
-/
theorem accepts_infinite_of_long {x : List α} (hx : x ∈ M.accepts)
    (hlen : Fintype.card σ ≤ x.length) :
    M.accepts.Infinite := by
  -- By the pumping lemma, we can decompose x into a = a ++ b ++ c where b is non-empty and a ++ b i ++ c is accepted for all i ≥ 0.
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, hx_eq, hb_nonempty, h_accept⟩ : ∃ a b c : List α, x = a ++ b ++ c ∧ b ≠ [] ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, a ++ List.flatten (List.replicate i b) ++ c ∈ M.accepts := by
    obtain ⟨ a, b, c, h₁, h₂, h₃ ⟩ := M.pumping_lemma hx hlen;
    refine' ⟨ a, b, c, h₁, h₃.1, fun i => h₃.2 _ ⟩;
    grind +suggestions;
  refine Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem ( fun i j hij => ?_ ) h_accept;

    exact ⟨v.1, hv, by rw [v.2]; exact n.2⟩
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, hlt⟩
    exact ⟨⟨x.length, hlt⟩, ⟨x, rfl⟩, hx⟩

This cycle formalized the automata-theoretic core of the "halting problem for
automatic sequences": the zero-in-sequence problem reduces to DFA language
emptiness, which a pumping/pigeonhole argument collapses to a *finite* search

infinitude dichotomy (`accepts_infinite_of_long`, `zero_value_infinite`).  We

## C1. Sharp pumping threshold for the zero set is exactly the state count
**Conjecture.** For a DFAO with `s` states and output map `out`, the set
`{w | out (M.eval w) = z}` is infinite **iff** it contains a word of length in the
window `[s, 2s)`; equivalently, finiteness is decided by inspecting words of
length `< s` only, and infinitude by exhibiting one in `[s, 2s)`.

**The key insight is** that `DFA.pumping_lemma` already localizes the loop `b`
inside the first `s` letters (`a.length + b.length ≤ s`), so the entire
finite/infinite dichotomy is witnessed within a bounded length window rather than
unboundedly far out.

**Why now?** We have machine-checked both halves of the dichotomy
(`accepts_finite_iff` and `accepts_infinite_of_long`); tightening the witness
length from "≥ s" to the explicit window `[s, 2s)` is a finite combinatorial
refinement that our existing pumping infrastructure should discharge.

## C2. Eventual periodicity generalizes from unary to ultimately-constant inputs
**Conjecture.** If the representation stream `repr n` is eventually constant in
its tail letter (reads a fixed letter `a` after a bounded prefix), then
`n ↦ out (M.eval (repr n))` is eventually periodic, with period dividing the
order of `s ↦ M.step s a` in `Function.End σ`.

**The key insight is** that `unary_autoSeq_eventually_periodic` already shows the
tail dynamics are governed by a single endofunction's orbit; a bounded prefix only
shifts the starting state, leaving the eventual period intact.

**Why now?** `End_pow_apply` + `evalFrom_replicate` give an exact bridge between
list evaluation and monoid powers, so the prefix-shift argument is within reach of
the same `pow_eventually_periodic` engine we already invoked.

## C3. Finite-valuedness is the decisive separator: automatic ⊊ P-recursive
**Conjecture.** Every `k`-automatic integer sequence is `P`-recursive, but the
converse fails on exactly the unbounded `P`-recursive sequences; a `P`-recursive
sequence is automatic only if it takes finitely many values.

**The key insight is** that `autoSeq_range_finite` makes finite range a *necessary*
condition for automaticity, and `id_not_automatic` shows the simplest unbounded

**Why now?** We have a formal, axiom-clean obstruction (`autoSeq_range_finite`);
the remaining task is to formalize the `automatic ⟹ P-recursive` direction and the
finite-range converse, both of which are structural rather than analytic.

**Conjecture.** The zero-in-sequence problem stays decidable for morphic
sequences generated by morphisms whose iterated images have lengths obeying a
linear recurrence (a strict subclass of general morphic sequences), via a pumping
argument on the substitution graph rather than the DFA.

finiteness of the state set plus a loop; a length-uniform morphism induces a
finite "block automaton" whose loops admit the same down-pump/up-pump dichotomy.

foundational, step — letting us probe precisely where decidability breaks toward
the general (open) morphic case.

# Information-Theoretic Limits of Proof Search: How Hard Is It to Find a Lean Proof?

This file develops an abstract, fully formal account of the *information-theoretic*
obstructions to finding proofs by search. The guiding question is operational: a
mechanical prover that searches for a proof of a statement enumerates candidate
proof objects (strings, terms, tactic scripts) and runs a *verifier* on each. How
large is this search, and what does the size of the search space tell us about the
distribution of "easy" versus "hard" theorems?

## Model

* An **alphabet** of size `a` is modelled by `Fin a` (e.g. the tokens of a proof
  language). A **proof of length `n`** is a string `Fin n → Fin a` (`ProofStr`).
* A **bounded search space** `BoundedProof a L` collects every proof string of
  length `≤ L` as a dependent sum `Σ n : Fin (L+1), ProofStr a n`.
* A **verifier** is *any* function `check : BoundedProof a L → S` assigning to each
  candidate proof the statement it certifies. (Totality loses no generality: route
  "rejected" strings to a junk statement.) A statement `s` is **provable within
  budget `L`** iff some candidate verifies to `s`, i.e. `s ∈ range check`.

## Main results

* `proofStr_card` / `boundedProof_card` — exact sizes of the search spaces:
  `a ^ n` and `∑ k ≤ L, a ^ k`.
* `boundedProof_card_lt` — the bounded search space has size `< a ^ (L+1)`
  (the *exponential search wall*).
* `provable_card_lt` — **counting limit**: a verifier with budget `L` can certify
  fewer than `a ^ (L+1)` distinct statements, no matter how clever it is.
* `exists_unprovable` — **incompressibility**: if there are at least `a ^ (L+1)`
  distinct statements, some statement is unprovable within budget `L`.
* `length_lower_bound` — **proof-length lower bound**: certifying `N` distinct
  statements forces budget `L ≥ log_a N`; equivalently the minimal proof length
  grows at least logarithmically in the number of theorems, so the brute-force
  search space grows at least linearly in `N`.
* `provable_fraction_lt` — **vanishing density**: among `M` candidate statements,
  the provable fraction is `< a^(L+1) / M`, exponentially small in `M`'s bit-length
  relative to the budget.

See the `-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--` blocks throughout for the hypotheses we tested,
what worked, and the dead ends. The headline finding: *the hardness of proof search
is governed by a single clean inequality* — the number of certifiable theorems is
bounded by the size of the search space, which is exponential in the proof-length
budget. Everything else (incompressibility, log lower bounds, vanishing density) is
a corollary of this one counting fact.

namespace ProofSearchLimits

open Finset

/-! ## Section 1: The search space -/

/-- A proof string of length `n` over an alphabet of size `a`. -/
abbrev ProofStr (a n : ℕ) := Fin n → Fin a

/-- The bounded search space: every proof string of length `≤ L`. -/
abbrev BoundedProof (a L : ℕ) := Σ n : Fin (L + 1), ProofStr a (n : ℕ)

!-- Lab Notes -- !--

This is the cleanest possible "exponential branching" statement and underpins
everything. Modelling proofs as `Fin n → Fin a` (rather than `List`) made the
cardinality computations one-liners via `Fintype.card_fun`; the `List`-with-
bounded-length encoding was a dead end (no clean `Fintype.card`).
!-- End Lab Notes -- !--

The fixed-length search space `ProofStr a n` has exactly `a ^ n` candidates.
-/
theorem proofStr_card (a n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (ProofStr a n) = a ^ n := by
  simp +decide [ ProofStr ]

/-
The bounded search space is the geometric sum `∑ k ≤ L, a ^ k`.
-/
theorem boundedProof_card (a L : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (BoundedProof a L) = ∑ k ∈ range (L + 1), a ^ k := by
  rw [ Fintype.card_sigma, Finset.sum_range ];
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun _ _ => proofStr_card _ _ ▸ rfl

/-
!-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis H2 (the "exponential search wall"): the whole budget-`L` search space
still fits strictly under `a^(L+1)`. We require `a ≥ 2` (a degenerate one-symbol
alphabet proves nothing interesting and breaks the bound: `∑ 1 = L+1 > 1 = 1^?`).
`Nat.geomSum_lt` discharged this immediately once stated with `range (L+1)`.
!-- End Lab Notes -- !--

**Exponential search wall.** For a nontrivial alphabet (`a ≥ 2`), the entire
budget-`L` search space has fewer than `a ^ (L+1)` candidates.
-/
theorem boundedProof_card_lt (a L : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a) :
    Fintype.card (BoundedProof a L) < a ^ (L + 1) := by
  rw [ boundedProof_card ] ; exact Nat.geomSum_lt ha ( by aesop ) ;

/-! ## Section 2: The counting limit on provability -/

variable {S : Type*}

/-- A statement is provable within budget `L` under verifier `check` iff some
candidate proof string verifies to it. -/
def Provable (a L : ℕ) (check : BoundedProof a L → S) (s : S) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, check p = s

/-
!-- Lab Notes -- !--

certify `a^(L+1)` or more distinct statements within budget `L`. The proof is a
pigeonhole: the provable statements are the image of `check`, and an image is no
larger than its (finite) domain, which is `< a^(L+1)` by H2. We phrase the

generated stray `Set.Finite` obligations.
!-- End Lab Notes -- !--

certifies fewer than `a ^ (L+1)` distinct statements.
-/
theorem provable_card_lt [DecidableEq S] (a L : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a)
    (check : BoundedProof a L → S) :
    (univ.image check).card < a ^ (L + 1) := by
  refine' lt_of_le_of_lt _ ( boundedProof_card_lt a L ha );
  exact Finset.card_image_le.trans_eq ( Finset.card_univ )

The set of statements provable within budget `L` is exactly the image of the
verifier (a `Finset` since the search space is finite).

    a ^ L ≤ Fintype.card (BoundedProof a L) := by

budget `L` that certifies exactly `Fintype.card (BoundedProof a L)` distinct
statements — namely the identity verifier, every proof string proving "itself".

    ∃ (T : Type) (_ : Fintype T) (_ : DecidableEq T) (check : BoundedProof a L → T),
      (Finset.univ.image check).card = Fintype.card (BoundedProof a L) := by
  use BoundedProof a L;
  refine' ⟨ inferInstance, inferInstance, _, _ ⟩;

/-
# Eulerian trails: the classical parity theorem

A small, self-contained development of the parity (handshake-style) theorem for
Eulerian trails in finite undirected multigraphs **with loops**.

## Model

* `Multigraph nV nE` is a finite multigraph on vertex set `Fin nV` with edge set
  `Fin nE`, given by two endpoint maps `endpt₁ endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV`.
  A loop is an edge `e` with `endpt₁ e = endpt₂ e`.

* `degree G v` counts endpoint incidences at `v`, summing over **both** endpoint
  slots; hence a loop at `v` contributes `2`.

* `Trail G` is an Eulerian trail: a vertex walk `verts : Fin (nE+1) → Fin nV`
  together with a permutation `edgePerm` of the edges (so every edge is used
  exactly once) and a proof `adj` that the `i`-th step traverses edge
  `edgePerm i` between `verts i.castSucc` and `verts i.succ`, in either
  orientation.

## Main results

1. `Trail.parity_identity` — the local counting identity at every vertex `v`:
   `degree G v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * visitCount v`.
   The proof is pure finite counting: each internal visit contributes two
   incidences, each endpoint one.

2. `Trail.odd_degree_isEndpoint` — if `Odd (degree G v)` then `v` is the start
   or the end vertex of the trail.

3. `Trail.card_oddDegree_le_two` — at most two vertices have odd degree.

4. `Trail.closed_even_degree` — if the trail is closed (start = end) then every
   vertex has even degree.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace EulerianParity

open Finset

/-- A finite undirected multigraph with loops: vertices `Fin nV`, edges `Fin nE`,
and two endpoint maps. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  endpt₁ : Fin nE → Fin nV
  endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of `v`: the number of endpoint incidences equal to `v`, counting
both endpoint slots. A loop at `v` contributes `2`. -/
def degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₁ e = v)).card +
  (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₂ e = v)).card

/-- An Eulerian trail: a vertex walk using every edge exactly once. -/
structure Trail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  /-- The walk of `nE + 1` vertices. -/
  verts : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  /-- The order in which the edges are traversed (each edge exactly once). -/
  edgePerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin nE)
  /-- Step `i` traverses edge `edgePerm i` between consecutive walk vertices,
  in either orientation. -/
  adj : ∀ i : Fin nE,
      (G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts i.castSucc ∧ G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ) ∨
      (G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ ∧ G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts i.castSucc)

namespace Trail

variable {G : Multigraph nV nE}

/-- The starting vertex of the trail. -/
def start (T : Trail G) : Fin nV := T.verts 0

/-- The ending vertex of the trail. -/
def last (T : Trail G) : Fin nV := T.verts (Fin.last nE)

/-- The number of times the walk visits `v` (over all `nE + 1` positions). -/
def visitCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ j : Fin (nE + 1), (if T.verts j = v then 1 else 0)

/-- `1` if `v` is the start vertex, else `0`. -/
def startIndicator (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts 0 = v then 1 else 0

/-- `1` if `v` is the end vertex, else `0`. -/
def endIndicator (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts (Fin.last nE) = v then 1 else 0

/-- Count of steps whose *first* (castSucc) walk vertex equals `v`. -/
def castCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin nE, (if T.verts i.castSucc = v then 1 else 0)

/-- Count of steps whose *second* (succ) walk vertex equals `v`. -/
def succCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin nE, (if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0)

variable (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV)

/-
Splitting the walk at its last vertex.
-/
lemma visit_eq_cast_add_end : T.visitCount v = T.castCount v + T.endIndicator v := by
  unfold Trail.visitCount Trail.castCount Trail.endIndicator; rw [ Fin.sum_univ_castSucc ] ;

/-
Splitting the walk at its first vertex.
-/
lemma visit_eq_start_add_succ : T.visitCount v = T.startIndicator v + T.succCount v := by
  convert Fin.sum_univ_succ _

/-
The degree of `v` equals the number of consecutive walk pairs incident to
`v` (first slot plus second slot). This is where the edge permutation and the
adjacency condition are used.
-/
lemma degree_eq_cast_add_succ : degree G v = T.castCount v + T.succCount v := by
  -- By definition of degree, we can express it as the sum over the edges of the number of times the vertex appears as an endpoint.
  have h_deg : degree G v = ∑ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ e = v then 1 else 0) + ∑ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₂ e = v then 1 else 0) := by
    unfold degree; aesop;
  have h_perm : ∀ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ (T.edgePerm e) = v then 1 else 0) + (if G.endpt₂ (T.edgePerm e) = v then 1 else 0) = (if T.verts e.castSucc = v then 1 else 0) + (if T.verts e.succ = v then 1 else 0) := by
    intro e; rcases T.adj e with h|h <;> simp +decide [ h ] ;
    ring;
  convert Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ => h_perm e using 1;
  any_goals exact Finset.univ;
  · convert h_deg using 1;
    rw [ Finset.sum_add_distrib, Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm fun e => if G.endpt₁ e = v then 1 else 0, Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm fun e => if G.endpt₂ e = v then 1 else 0 ];
  · unfold Trail.castCount Trail.succCount; simp +decide [ Finset.sum_add_distrib ] ;

/-- **Local parity identity.** At every vertex `v`:
`degree G v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * visitCount v`. -/
theorem parity_identity :
    degree G v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v = 2 * T.visitCount v := by
  have hd := T.degree_eq_cast_add_succ v
  have h1 := T.visit_eq_cast_add_end v
  have h2 := T.visit_eq_start_add_succ v
  omega

/-- If `v` has odd degree, then it is the start or the end vertex of the trail. -/
theorem odd_degree_isEndpoint (h : Odd (degree G v)) :
    v = T.start ∨ v = T.last := by
  obtain ⟨ k, hk ⟩ := h;
  have := parity_identity T v; simp_all +decide [ Nat.even_iff ];
  unfold Trail.startIndicator Trail.endIndicator at this;
  unfold Trail.start Trail.last; split_ifs at this <;> omega;

/-- The set of odd-degree vertices has cardinality at most `2` (the existence of
the Eulerian trail `T` is essential). -/
theorem card_oddDegree_le_two (T : Trail G) :
    (univ.filter (fun v => Odd (degree G v))).card ≤ 2 := by
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card ( show Finset.filter ( fun v => Odd ( degree G v ) ) Finset.univ ⊆ { T.start, T.last } from fun v hv => by have := odd_degree_isEndpoint ( T := T ) ( v := v ) ( Finset.mem_filter.mp hv |>.2 ) ; aesop ) ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

theorem closed_even_degree (hclosed : T.start = T.last) (v : Fin nV) :

  have hid := T.parity_identity v;

end Trail

end EulerianParity

# Eulerian trails: the classical parity theorem

A small, self-contained development of the parity (handshake-style) theorem for
Eulerian trails in finite undirected multigraphs **with loops**.

## Model

* `Multigraph nV nE` is a finite multigraph on vertex set `Fin nV` with edge set
  `Fin nE`, given by two endpoint maps `endpt₁ endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV`.
  A loop is an edge `e` with `endpt₁ e = endpt₂ e`.

* `degree G v` counts endpoint incidences at `v`, summing over **both** endpoint
  slots; hence a loop at `v` contributes `2`.

* `Trail G` is an Eulerian trail: a vertex walk `verts : Fin (nE+1) → Fin nV`
  together with a permutation `edgePerm` of the edges (so every edge is used
  exactly once) and a proof `adj` that the `i`-th step traverses edge
  `edgePerm i` between `verts i.castSucc` and `verts i.succ`, in either
  orientation.

## Main results

1. `Trail.parity_identity` — the local counting identity at every vertex `v`:
   `degree G v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * visitCount v`.
   The proof is pure finite counting: each internal visit contributes two
   incidences, each endpoint one.

2. `Trail.odd_degree_isEndpoint` — if `Odd (degree G v)` then `v` is the start
   or the end vertex of the trail.

3. `Trail.card_oddDegree_le_two` — at most two vertices have odd degree.

4. `Trail.closed_even_degree` — if the trail is closed (start = end) then every
   vertex has even degree.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace EulerianParity

open Finset

/-- A finite undirected multigraph with loops: vertices `Fin nV`, edges `Fin nE`,
and two endpoint maps. -/
structure Multigraph (nV nE : ℕ) where
  endpt₁ : Fin nE → Fin nV
  endpt₂ : Fin nE → Fin nV

variable {nV nE : ℕ}

/-- The degree of `v`: the number of endpoint incidences equal to `v`, counting
both endpoint slots. A loop at `v` contributes `2`. -/
def degree (G : Multigraph nV nE) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₁ e = v)).card +
  (univ.filter (fun e => G.endpt₂ e = v)).card

/-- An Eulerian trail: a vertex walk using every edge exactly once. -/
structure Trail (G : Multigraph nV nE) where
  /-- The walk of `nE + 1` vertices. -/
  verts : Fin (nE + 1) → Fin nV
  /-- The order in which the edges are traversed (each edge exactly once). -/
  edgePerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin nE)
  /-- Step `i` traverses edge `edgePerm i` between consecutive walk vertices,
  in either orientation. -/
  adj : ∀ i : Fin nE,
      (G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts i.castSucc ∧ G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ) ∨
      (G.endpt₁ (edgePerm i) = verts i.succ ∧ G.endpt₂ (edgePerm i) = verts i.castSucc)

namespace Trail

variable {G : Multigraph nV nE}

/-- The starting vertex of the trail. -/
def start (T : Trail G) : Fin nV := T.verts 0

/-- The ending vertex of the trail. -/
def last (T : Trail G) : Fin nV := T.verts (Fin.last nE)

/-- The number of times the walk visits `v` (over all `nE + 1` positions). -/
def visitCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ j : Fin (nE + 1), (if T.verts j = v then 1 else 0)

/-- `1` if `v` is the start vertex, else `0`. -/
def startIndicator (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts 0 = v then 1 else 0

/-- `1` if `v` is the end vertex, else `0`. -/
def endIndicator (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  if T.verts (Fin.last nE) = v then 1 else 0

/-- Count of steps whose *first* (castSucc) walk vertex equals `v`. -/
def castCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin nE, (if T.verts i.castSucc = v then 1 else 0)

/-- Count of steps whose *second* (succ) walk vertex equals `v`. -/
def succCount (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin nE, (if T.verts i.succ = v then 1 else 0)

variable (T : Trail G) (v : Fin nV)

/-
Splitting the walk at its last vertex.
-/
lemma visit_eq_cast_add_end : T.visitCount v = T.castCount v + T.endIndicator v := by
  unfold Trail.visitCount Trail.castCount Trail.endIndicator; rw [ Fin.sum_univ_castSucc ] ;

/-
Splitting the walk at its first vertex.
-/
lemma visit_eq_start_add_succ : T.visitCount v = T.startIndicator v + T.succCount v := by
  convert Fin.sum_univ_succ _

/-
The degree of `v` equals the number of consecutive walk pairs incident to
`v` (first slot plus second slot). This is where the edge permutation and the
adjacency condition are used.
-/
lemma degree_eq_cast_add_succ : degree G v = T.castCount v + T.succCount v := by
  -- By definition of degree, we can express it as the sum over the edges of the number of times the vertex appears as an endpoint.
  have h_deg : degree G v = ∑ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ e = v then 1 else 0) + ∑ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₂ e = v then 1 else 0) := by
    unfold degree; aesop;
  have h_perm : ∀ e : Fin nE, (if G.endpt₁ (T.edgePerm e) = v then 1 else 0) + (if G.endpt₂ (T.edgePerm e) = v then 1 else 0) = (if T.verts e.castSucc = v then 1 else 0) + (if T.verts e.succ = v then 1 else 0) := by
    intro e; rcases T.adj e with h|h <;> simp +decide [ h ] ;
    ring;
  convert Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e _ => h_perm e using 1;
  any_goals exact Finset.univ;
  · convert h_deg using 1;
    rw [ Finset.sum_add_distrib, Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm fun e => if G.endpt₁ e = v then 1 else 0, Equiv.sum_comp T.edgePerm fun e => if G.endpt₂ e = v then 1 else 0 ];
  · unfold Trail.castCount Trail.succCount; simp +decide [ Finset.sum_add_distrib ] ;

/-- **Local parity identity.** At every vertex `v`:
`degree G v + startIndicator v + endIndicator v = 2 * visitCount v`. -/
theorem parity_identity :
    degree G v + T.startIndicator v + T.endIndicator v = 2 * T.visitCount v := by
  have hd := T.degree_eq_cast_add_succ v
  have h1 := T.visit_eq_cast_add_end v
  have h2 := T.visit_eq_start_add_succ v
  omega

/-- If `v` has odd degree, then it is the start or the end vertex of the trail. -/
theorem odd_degree_isEndpoint (h : Odd (degree G v)) :
    v = T.start ∨ v = T.last := by
  obtain ⟨ k, hk ⟩ := h;
  have := parity_identity T v; simp_all +decide [ Nat.even_iff ];
  unfold Trail.startIndicator Trail.endIndicator at this;
  unfold Trail.start Trail.last; split_ifs at this <;> omega;

/-- The set of odd-degree vertices has cardinality at most `2` (the existence of
the Eulerian trail `T` is essential). -/
theorem card_oddDegree_le_two (T : Trail G) :
    (univ.filter (fun v => Odd (degree G v))).card ≤ 2 := by
  exact le_trans ( Finset.card_le_card ( show Finset.filter ( fun v => Odd ( degree G v ) ) Finset.univ ⊆ { T.start, T.last } from fun v hv => by have := odd_degree_isEndpoint ( T := T ) ( v := v ) ( Finset.mem_filter.mp hv |>.2 ) ; aesop ) ) ( Finset.card_insert_le _ _ )

/-- If the trail is closed (start equals end), every vertex has even degree. -/
theorem closed_even_degree (hclosed : T.start = T.last) (v : Fin nV) :
    Even (degree G v) := by
  have hid := T.parity_identity v;
  grind +locals

end Trail

end EulerianParity
